subject: Recap & next steps: Procurement path for Redwood trial / PO vs card
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps: Procurement path for Redwood trial / PO vs card

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on procurement and the commercial path: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Acme is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing summarization and support routing (prod trial with ~5M tokens/mo).
- Procurement prefers PO-based purchases for any vendor over $10k/mo and has a formal paper process; card purchases are only for subscriptions under that threshold.
- There’s interest in using the GCP marketplace, but procurement needs to confirm marketplace terms and invoicing cadence first.

Questions / asks we had (so we can move to procurement):
1) Can you confirm the budget owner / economic buyer for this workload (name & email)?
2) Who in procurement/legal will be the signatory for an SOW or subscription?
3) Any required billing/legal terms beyond a standard Redwood SaaS MSA (e.g., data residency, SOC 2 attestation)?
4) Expected procurement timeline (weeks) and PO approval SLA.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa/Aditya: share a draft SOW + pricing options (PO vs card) and a sample PO template by EOD today. (ACTION: Marissa)
- Acme: confirm budget owner and procurement contact; indicate whether marketplace listing would simplify purchase.
- Align on a short call next week with Liam (Finance) and procurement to walk the SOW and timelines.

I’ve attached a one-page SOW draft and pricing sheet for the 3-month trial. Happy to adjust.

Thanks — talk soon.
—
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (one-page trial SOW, pricing matrix)

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme.com>

Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Procurement path for Redwood trial / PO vs card

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Confirmed: procurement will require a PO for any spend expected to exceed $10k/month. For a short 3-month pilot if we expect to be at ~5M tokens/mo, that will likely be above that threshold and will need the PO route.
- Budget owner / economic buyer: Liam O'Connor (VP Finance) — liam.oconnor@acme.com. He will sign off on budget and capex/opex classification.
- Procurement contact: procurement@acme.com handles PO processing and will need the invoice remit details; procurement team will also validate marketplace invoicing if we go that route.
- Signatory: Legal typically signs SOWs > $50k; for pilots they sometimes allow the business owner to sign, but we’ll need legal (Nina Patel, CLO) to approve final terms. I put Nina on copy for visibility.

Timeline: procurement estimates ~2–3 weeks once we have an approved SOW + pricing and a PO form. If Redwood is available on the GCP marketplace with standard invoicing, that can shave a week off the process.

I’ll coordinate with Liam and procurement and follow up with a proposed time for a quick alignment call next Tue/Wed.

—
Sofia Ramos
Director, Product Management (AI)
Acme Corp

Subject: RE: Recap & next steps: Procurement path for Redwood trial / PO vs card

Hi Sofia — adding a couple quick options to make this easier from a procurement perspective:

Option A (PO):
- Standard PO + monthly invoicing (net 30). We can accept Acme PO and process through our finance team.
- We’ll ship a short SOW outlining trial scope and a single subscription invoice per month.

Option B (Card / CC):
- Card is supported but would require a smaller pilot (< $10k/mo) or use a Redwood prepaid credit if you want to keep procurement out of the loop.

Option C (Marketplace):
- If Acme wants to purchase via GCP marketplace, our team can connect you to our marketplace onboarding contact. Marketplace invoicing tends to be standard 30-day and can simplify approvals, but it depends on internal procurement acceptance.

I’m attaching a very short SOW + pricing matrix for the pilot and a sample invoicing template we normally include with PO deals. Happy to walk through any of these on the call.

—
Aditya Rao
